decisions.reason: As a newly launched particle-therapy water phantom that fits the firm's core QA platform strategy, its value is still unresolved in 2019 and the staged rollout signal suggests management would preserve the option rather than exit early.

This small volume ionization chamber is a close extension of the firm's established dosimetry business, so with little time for market learning and no negative signal, keeping it open is the low-regret real-options choice.

Because this newly launched small volume ionization chamber sits squarely within the firm's technical capabilities and customer base, management would continue offering it while demand and differentiation become clearer.

A standard clinical ionization chamber is highly complementary to the firm's existing measurement portfolio, and in the absence of poor market evidence the option value of staying in the market exceeds the likely carrying cost.
The relative dosimetry chamber strengthens the firm's integrated radiotherapy QA offering, so a 2019 withdrawal would forfeit learning and cross-selling opportunities before uncertainty has resolved.
This thimble ionization chamber is an adjacent, capability-matched product with probable low ongoing support costs, making retention the sensible option until stronger performance evidence appears.
